clues: It equals the sum of inspiratory reserve volume, tidal volume, and expiratory reserve volume (~4,600 mL)
Unlike total lung capacity, it can be measured directly with a simple spirometer
It is the maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after a maximal inspiration
It averages ~1,200 mL in healthy adult males and increases markedly during air trapping in COPD
It cannot be measured by simple spirometry and requires gas dilution or body plethysmography
It is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a maximal forced expiration

terms.sub: Measurement of RV, FRC, and TLC
clues: It uses an insoluble inert tracer gas in a closed-circuit spirometer to compute unknown lung volume via C1V1 = C2V2
In bullous emphysema, it underestimates true lung volume because it only measures communicating airspaces
It is a classic gas-equilibration technique used to measure functional residual capacity

terms.sub: Measurement of RV, FRC, and TLC
clues: The patient sits inside an airtight chamber and pants against a closed shutter
It applies Boyle's law (P1V1 = P2V2) to measure total compressible thoracic gas volume
Unlike helium dilution, it includes non-communicating trapped bullous gas in emphysema

terms.sub: Dynamic Spirometry: FEV1, FVC, and FEF25-75%
clues: In healthy young adults, this index is normally 75 to 80 percent
It falls below 70 percent in obstructive diseases like asthma and COPD
It stays normal or rises above 80 percent in restrictive lung diseases

terms.sub: Dynamic Spirometry: FEV1, FVC, and FEF25-75%
clues: Also called maximal mid-expiratory flow rate, it is largely independent of patient effort
It is measured over the middle half of the forced vital capacity curve
It serves as a sensitive early marker of peripheral small-airway (<2 mm) obstruction

terms.sub: Peak Expiratory Flow Rate and Maximal Voluntary Ventilation
clues: It reaches ~500 to 700 L/min in healthy young adult males and is highly effort-dependent
It occurs near total lung capacity before dynamic airway compression begins
Patients with asthma measure it daily at home using a handheld meter to track green, yellow, and red zones

terms.sub: Peak Expiratory Flow Rate and Maximal Voluntary Ventilation
clues: It is measured by breathing as rapidly and deeply as possible for 12 to 15 seconds and extrapolating to 1 minute
Its normal adult male value (~125-170 L/min) approximates 35 to 40 times FEV1
Comparing it against maximal exercise minute ventilation determines a person's breathing reserve

terms.sub: Flow-Volume Loops and Airway Obstruction Patterns
clues: It plots instantaneous airflow on the vertical axis against lung volume on the horizontal axis during maximal expiration and inspiration
In COPD, its descending expiratory curve shows a characteristic concave 'scooped-out' shape
Flattening of its inspiratory, expiratory, or both limbs diagnoses variable versus fixed upper airway obstruction

terms.sub: Dynamic Spirometry: FEV1, FVC, and FEF25-75%
clues: It occurs when premature small-airway closure prevents complete alveolar emptying during expiration
It is quantified on PFTs by an elevated residual volume (>120% predicted) and increased RV/TLC ratio
It leads to hyperinflation in severe asthma and emphysema
